senses.definition: The immature young of a marsupial, notably a junior kangaroo, but also a young wallaby, koala, etc.

quotes.text: As soon as a joey is born, it crawls into its mother's pouch. The joey grows in the pouch.
quotes.reference: 2006, Bobbie Kalman, Robin R. Johnson, Koalas and Other Marsupials, Crabtree Publishing Company, →ISBN, page 9:

quotes.text: Among the kangaroo words that yield the most joviality and joy are those that conceal multiple joeys.
quotes.reference: 1998, Richard Lederer, Dave Morice, The Word Circus, page 129:

quotes.text: Sometimes a kangaroo word has more than one joey.
quotes.reference: 2005, Anu Garg, Another Word a Day, page 132:

senses.definition: (UK, Ireland, prison slang) A parcel smuggled in to an inmate.

quotes.text: "Visit in two days though," said Tommo. "Hang in there mate, got a joey coming, we'll be sweet then."
quotes.reference: 2012, John Hoskison, Inside: One Man's Experience of Prison:

senses.definition: (UK, military, slang) A member of the Royal Marines.
(dated, slang, derogatory, offensive in British) A person with cerebral palsy.
(dated, slang, derogatory, offensive in British) A stupid person.
(UK, slang, obsolete) A fourpenny piece, or its value; fourpence worth.
